reasons.vendor:
EVE-NG opnsense.yml (catalog-diff/eveng-catalog.md row 156): no
explicit -cpu flag - kept at qemu64 per row 38.9's rule.
nic corrected e1000 -> virtio-net-pci (Wave 38 row 38.12 live-boot pass,
2026-09-16, rule #59): EVE-NG's real opnsense.yml says
`qemu_nic: virtio-net-pci` - the earlier e1000 value was unexplained drift.
reasons.console:
console/day0: EVE-NG's own real opnsense.yml says `console: vnc` (its
`-serial mon:stdio` flag only carries early boot-loader chatter, not the
interactive console) - this is a DELIBERATE, evidenced deviation (rule #59),
not drift: EVE-NG's own image is the plain "vga" OPNsense build, which has
no real interactive serial console at all (the same class of gap NPX-1200
already found and fixed for pfSense). netplex instead uses OPNsense's own
official "serial" build variant (`OPNsense-<ver>-serial-amd64.img`, a
ready-made raw disk image, sha256-verified against the vendor's own
published checksum before import) - a real, current, upstream-supported
build with a genuine interactive serial getty, matching this project's own
console-relay design (same "just use the vendor's serial build" choice
the project owner directed for pfSense). Live-confirmed 2026-09-16: this build's
console is genuinely interactive over telnet (a live boot reached the
BSD kernel boot menu on the real console, not silence).
